## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (99%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Single-class conformal set, second model agrees, input not flagged [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 99%, InSitu 1% | Clear leader |
| Conformal set | Benign only | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.999 / 1.0 | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 Benign | Mostly supportive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↓ invasive · Below typical; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 2, 4, 8) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Weak
- **Scarce benign stroma/fat** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Small push toward invasive; outweighed by opposing terms [F4] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 1, 11) · ↓ invasive · Positive score; associated with lower invasive likelihood · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Deleting the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60): faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect classifier use. Mitoses, normal lobules and necrosis are Unreliable (≤3/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Region 9 holds focal invasive tumor: its per-region probe risk is 92%, versus 0% overall.
- Image is JPEG-degraded (severity 3); reliability score ranks errors only modestly (AUROC 0.69).

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 9**: confirm no invasive focus; per-region probe risk is 92%.
2. **Region 3**: look for infiltrating tumor in stroma; top region for that concept.
3. **Regions 2, 4, 8**: look for atypical ductal cells; InSitu is the runner-up (1%).
